meta: The 7,341-row sales log of the bubble tea shop from video 301, handed straight to Claude inside Excel. Every table and chart is a real Excel file it made: it catches a double-count, summarizes and forecasts with formulas.
thu: ask Claude to find 3 unusual things in a copy of your spending or sales file.

muc.title: A 7,341-row sales log
muc.text: Remember the bubble tea shop's sales log of more than 7,000 rows from Mark's aunt in video 301? This time we give that exact file to Claude, and every table and chart you're about to see is a real Excel file it made.

muc.title: An add-in inside Excel
muc.text: To use it right inside Excel, install the Claude for Microsoft 365 add-in from Microsoft Marketplace, then go to the Home tab, choose Add-ins and click Claude. The add-in runs on Excel for the web, Windows and Mac, and needs a paid plan, Pro or higher.

muc.title: What's the real total?
muc.text: The first question was the total revenue for three months, and Claude didn't just add up the whole column, because it noticed three monthly total rows mixed into the data. Adding everything would give almost 587 million, double the correct figure of 293 million.

muc.title: By item, by month
muc.text: Next, ask it to summarize revenue by item and by month, color the items going up and down, then draw a column chart. Taro milk tea fell 57 percent, while peach lemongrass tea rose 42 percent.

muc.title: Change a number, it recalculates
muc.text: Then ask Claude to build an October forecast sheet with formulas, with one growth-rate cell for peach tea. Change that cell from 5 to 10 percent and the forecast total jumps from about 96 million to nearly 97.3 million, because the formulas stay intact instead of being overwritten with numbers.

muc.title: Work on a copy
muc.text: According to Anthropic's guidance, Claude asks before overwriting data and can't do macros yet. Work on a copy, and only open files you trust, because unfamiliar files can hide instructions.

muc.title: The Instructions box
muc.text: In the add-in's Settings there's an Instructions box where you write your habits once, like using dots as thousands separators, so it does it your way every time.

muc.title: Three unusual things
muc.text: Take a copy of one of your spending or sales files and ask Claude to find three unusual things and point to exactly which cells they're in.

muc.title: Next: PowerPoint
muc.text: Part 3: take these results straight into PowerPoint as a five-slide staff meeting deck, without copying a single number.
